subject: Arabic

source: Written for arabic/y7 lesson 10 (Vowel and sign cards; dictation sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 10: Bridge: short vowels, sukun, shaddah and tanwin. Read the Arabic aloud, then do the tasks. Write in Arabic with all the harakat.

cards:
فَتْحَة
fathah
a short 'a' mark above the l

ضَمَّة
dammah
a short 'u' mark above the l

كَسْرَة
kasrah
a short 'i' mark below the l

تَنْوِين
tanwin
a double mark adding -n
blocks.task: say the Arabic, turn over and check, or play pairs with a partner.

box.title: Write the words your teacher says, with all the harakat

keywords.def: a short 'a' mark above the letter
a short 'u' mark above the letter
a short 'i' mark below the letter

questions.q: Which mark makes the letter double?
Core: Dictation of six vowelled words (كَتَبَ، كُتُبٌ، مِنْ، رَبّ، مُدَرِّسٌ، بَابًا), then read them aloud to the teacher.
questions.a: كَتَبَ، كُتُبٌ، مِنْ، رَبّ، مُدَرِّسٌ، بَابًا

questions.q: Extend: Add the vowels you hear: محمد (Muhammad), مسجد (masjid).
Stretch: Write كِتَاب with each tanwin and say when each might be used.
questions.a: كِتَابٌ، كِتَابًا، كِتَابٍ: they show the word's job in the sentence (subject, object, after a preposition)
B) rabb. Fathah on ر gives ra; the shaddah on ب doubles it: rabb.

questions.q: Which mark means 'no vowel'? A) fathah B) sukun C) kasrah
Big question: how do the small marks change how a word sounds? Give one example.
questions.a: They give the vowels; e.g. كَتَبَ (kataba) and كُتُب (kutub) have the same letters but different vowels.
